results.title: Probabilistic sensitivity analysis and value of information ...
results.content: The Second Panel on Cost-Effectiveness in Health and Medicine notes that PSA is a more thorough approach for quantifying the uncertainty inherent in decision modelling (Sanders et al., 2016). This decision tree model estimates the cost-effectiveness of vaccinating elderly individuals. In each iteration, input parameters for the model were pulled from respective probability distributions and led to varying estimates for the cost-effectiveness of the vaccine. Confidence intervals and p-values can be derived for cost-effectiveness estimates in decision modelling studies through PSA. This information can be used to elicit the probability of making an incorrect decision based on model results and estimate the value of reducing uncertainty in the decision. As we increase the number of PSA runs and average over observed outcomes, our cost-effectiveness estimate tends towards the expected value of the model. These include reporting expected values derived from simulations, reporting uncertainty intervals for estimates, and visually presenting results in scatter plots and cost-effectiveness acceptability curves. doi:10.1111/j.1524-4733.2008.00502.x. Handling uncertainty in cost-effectiveness models.
